name: Jeddah
title: Thickness Measurement Jeddah | Red Sea Ship UTM & Gauging
description: UTM in Jeddah Islamic Port for container ships, tankers and bulk carriers: hull structure gauging, scrubber piping inspection and pre-docking checks.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement and Ship Inspection in Jeddah
intro: Jeddah Islamic Port is Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea gateway, handling container, bulk, ro-ro and tanker traffic at the centre of the route between Suez and the Bab el-Mandeb. When a ship calling at Jeddah needs gauging before a survey, a docking or a charter, we send a team from India, obtain the visas and port passes, and work alongside or at anchor around the ship's cargo programme.
keywords: ballast tank gauging in the red sea

highlights.p: Jeddah sits roughly midway along the Red Sea, where ships on the Suez route, Saudi import cargoes and regional transhipment meet. For some services it is the only stop between Suez and the Gulf of Aden, and so a natural gauging window.

Red Sea water is among the warmest seawater ships routinely carry as ballast, and warmth speeds corrosion wherever tank coatings have broken down. Ballast tank gauging on ships trading here regularly is worth planning at every survey.

Saudi port access needs a visa for each technician and a port pass arranged through the ship's agent. We start both as soon as the ETA or docking window is known, so the team arrives at Jeddah with its paperwork complete.

port.h: Jeddah Islamic Port and its shipping
p: Jeddah Islamic Port, run under the Saudi Ports Authority, is the kingdom's main gateway on the Red Sea and one of the largest ports in the region. Its container terminals, including Red Sea Gateway Terminal, handle import cargo for western Saudi Arabia and transhipment for Red Sea and East African services. Alongside them are general cargo and ro-ro berths for vehicles and project cargo, grain berths and silos serving the kingdom's food imports, and tanker berths for refined products. The port also lies beside the main shipping lane between Suez and the Bab el-Mandeb, so Jeddah sees both ships that call and ships that simply pass.

For gauging, the useful windows come from cargo programmes and waiting time. Container ships alongside work to tight schedules but offer deck, coaming and scrubber piping access during the call; bulk carriers discharging grain end up with empty, clean holds; ro-ro ships have long vehicle decks whose plating and supporting structure can be measured once the cargo is out; and ships waiting at the anchorage outside the reef-lined approaches can be boarded by launch. Jeddah is also a sensible place to gauge before a docking elsewhere, since measurements taken here let a yard in the Gulf or at Suez prepare the steel list before the ship arrives.

Inspection demand, and the case for regular Red Sea ship thickness gauging, reflects the sea's conditions and its trades. Warm water speeds corrosion in ballast tanks where coatings have failed, which matters most for ships that spend nearly all their time in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden. Ro-ro ships and car carriers bringing vehicle imports carry long runs of deck plating and ramp structure that wear with every call. Container ships carry scrubbers whose wash-water piping needs monitoring, and the regional bulk and general cargo fleet includes older ships in the third and fourth renewal-survey bands.

Most gauging at Jeddah is done afloat, alongside or at anchor. The container terminals allow work on deck and in accessible tanks during cargo operations, within the terminal's ISPS and safety rules; the general cargo, ro-ro and bulk berths give fuller access once cargo is out; and the tanker berths allow deck and ballast work under terminal permits. Each terminal has its own induction and access procedure, which the ship's agent arranges. Heat matters too: tank entry in the Red Sea summer needs ventilation, rest breaks and work planning that a temperate port does not, and the gauging plan is written with that in mind.

The anchorage outside the port holds ships waiting for berths or orders, and boarding there is by launch booked through the agent, subject to harbour clearance. Where a ship is to dock at a yard elsewhere, Jeddah can be the last call before the yard where gauging fits without disrupting the voyage; measuring ballast tanks, holds and decks here gives the yard the figures to plan steel, staging and dock time. For ships in ballast between charters, the port can also be the place for on-hire or off-hire condition gauging, recording a baseline before the next employment begins.
list: Container terminals at Jeddah Islamic Port, including Red Sea Gateway Terminal — import and transhipment calls; scrubber lines, hatch coamings and deck plating measured during the call.
General cargo and ro-ro berths — vehicle and project cargo calls; vehicle deck, ramp and hold plating gauged once the cargo has been discharged.
Grain and bulk berths — food import cargoes; once discharge is complete, hold structure from tank top to upper frames can be measured.
Product tanker berths — refined fuel cargoes; measurement of deck plating, ballast tanks and deck lines within the terminal's permit system.
Jeddah anchorage — ships waiting for berths or orders outside the reefs; launch boarding for ballast tank, deck and hatch cover measurement.

context.h: Saudi port state control and the Red Sea operating context
p: Saudi Arabia inspects foreign ships under the Riyadh MoU, the regional port state control agreement of the Gulf Cooperation Council states, and Jeddah calls fall within it. With no ECA anywhere in the Red Sea, ships here work to the global 0.50% cap, and scrubber-fitted ships burning high-sulphur fuel keep their systems running for the whole passage. That makes scrubber piping inspection in Jeddah practical for ships moving between the Mediterranean ECA and the Indian Ocean, particularly where the same lines run in a more demanding mode north of Port Said.

Attacks on commercial ships near the Bab el-Mandeb, which began in November 2023, prompted many container lines and other operators to reroute via the Cape of Good Hope, changing which services call at Jeddah and how. Owners still trading through the Red Sea follow their own and their underwriters' security guidance; attendance at Jeddah is planned within that guidance, and the port itself lies well north of the strait. With King Abdullah Port and Yanbu to the north and Jazan to the south, a Jeddah mobilisation can be extended to other Saudi Red Sea ports whenever a fleet has ships spread along that coast.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Jeddah
jobs.p: Ships at Jeddah are usually working cargo, so the scope is fitted to what the cargo programme leaves open. The scenarios below are typical of the port's mix of container, ro-ro, bulk and tanker traffic, and every attendance is sized to the ship's survey status and what the terminal will allow. Heat, terminal rules and visa timing are built into the plan from the start.
list: Ballast tank gauging on a container feeder ship that trades only in the Red Sea, ahead of its intermediate survey, concentrating on tanks where coating breakdown was recorded.
A wall-thickness trend on the scrubber system of a large container ship at Red Sea Gateway Terminal, measuring wash-water and overboard lines between drydocks.
Vehicle deck, ramp and hold plating gauging on a ro-ro ship after discharging car imports, where wheel loading and trapped water have worn the deck plating.
Hold survey preparation on a bulk carrier that has just discharged grain at Jeddah: frames, brackets and hopper plating measured while the holds are empty, for a renewal survey later in the year.
A product tanker at the Jeddah anchorage gauged ahead of its docking, so the yard receives measured deck and ballast tank wastage before the ship sails.

logistics: The team arrives at King Abdulaziz International Airport, north of the city. Each technician needs a Saudi visa before travel from India, and the ship's agent applies for port passes for the people and the gauging equipment through the port's security system, using passport and visa details. For anchorage work, the agent arranges the launch and the boarding clearance. Because visa issue sets the earliest possible mobilisation date, the paperwork begins the moment the ETA, discharge window or docking date is firm, and keep the superintendent updated on progress.

faqs.q: Can you do ballast tank gauging in the Red Sea heat at Jeddah?
faqs.a: Yes, with the work planned for it. Tank entry in Red Sea temperatures needs good ventilation, gas testing, rest breaks and sensible scheduling, often with tank work early in the day. We agree the sequence with the chief officer so the team does not compete with cargo operations, and the gauging plan allows for slower progress in the hottest tanks.

faqs.q: Do you provide thickness measurement in Saudi Arabia outside Jeddah?
faqs.a: Yes. A Jeddah mobilisation can be extended to King Abdullah Port, Yanbu and Jazan on the Red Sea coast, and to Dammam and Jubail on the Gulf coast, subject to visas and the ships' schedules. Grouping several ships on one trip makes the best use of the visas and the travel from India.

faqs.q: Is Jeddah a good place to gauge before a docking elsewhere?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If the ship is heading for a yard in the Gulf or at Suez, gauging its ballast tanks, holds and decks in Jeddah gives the yard measured wastage ahead of arrival, so steel can be ordered and staging planned. In-dock items such as bottom plating and sea chests are then measured at the yard.

faqs.q: How does the Red Sea security situation affect ship inspection in Jeddah?
faqs.a: Jeddah lies well north of the Bab el-Mandeb, and in-port work is planned in the ordinary way. What has changed since late 2023 is which ships call: some services route around Africa while others continue through the Red Sea. We plan each attendance within the owner's security guidance and confirm arrangements with the agent before travel.
